content:
Mason: heads up — a bunch of customers in ap-southeast-1 just reported timeouts to models-api through the VPC endpoint after I merged the route-table cleanup PR. Private DNS still resolves but connections reset. Anyone seen this pattern before?

deploy-bot: route-table-update PR #482 merged by Mason at 12:10 UTC — author: mason — status: applied ✅

Priya: can you paste the dig +short output for models-api.internal.redwood from a prod-api pod in the affected cluster? want to confirm if it's resolving to vpce CNAME or direct ENI IPs

Mason: ran it from a pod (prod-api-7c9d):
```
$ dig +short models-api.internal.redwood @169.254.169.253
models-api.internal.redwood.cname.vpce-0a1b2c3d-abcde.ap-southeast-1.vpce.amazonaws.com.
10.0.5.23
10.0.6.19
```

Eli: ok that's the expected behavior (CNAME -> private IPs). Two quick checks: 1) are the endpoint ENIs healthy and still attached? 2) does the endpoint security group allow traffic from the cluster nat/ENI source IPs? run describe-network-interfaces filtered by those private IPs

Mason: pasted a minimal aws output from bastion:
```
$ aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=addresses.private-ip-address,Values=10.0.5.23
{
  "NetworkInterfaces": [
    {
      "NetworkInterfaceId": "eni-0f3b9a1c",
      "Status": "in-use",
      "Groups": [ { "GroupId": "sg-07a1b2c3" } ],
      "Attachment": { "InstanceOwnerId": "amazon-vpc-endpoint" }
    }]
}
```

Priya: what's sg-07a1b2c3's rules? if the endpoint SG only allows inbound from the VPC CIDR but the cluster traffic is coming via a NAT (different IP) the ENI will drop it. also double-check if the endpoint's hosted zone is associated with the cluster VPC — terraform sometimes loses that association on refactor.

Mason: ran quick sg describe: sg-07a1b2c3 only allows inbound TCP 443 from 10.0.0.0/16. our prod cluster pods are in 10.1.0.0/16 and go out via NAT gw in 10.2.5.14. hmm. the route-table PR removed an explicit route that pointed cluster subnet -> endpoint subnet earlier, so traffic may be SNATed by nat gw.

SRE-Robin: we had a similar incident last quarter — the hidden culprit was the VPC endpoint's private hosted zone association. If it's not associated to the VPC, DNS still resolves (because client sees CNAME) but the binding to the endpoint IPs can get stale across AZs and SG rules don't match. Run: 
```
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0a1b2c3d --query 'VpcEndpoints[0].{PrivateDnsEnabled:PrivateDnsEnabled,DnsEntries:DnsEntries,Associations:VpcEndpointOwnerId}'
```
and confirm HostedZoneId present and VpcEndpointId associations include the cluster VPC id.

Mason: confirmed output: PrivateDnsEnabled=true but HostedZoneId list is missing association for vpc-0c9d8e7f (our prod cluster). Looks like terraform removed the aws_route_table_association for the endpoint subnet and also the aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association for the cluster vpc during cleanup. Reverting PR now.

Priya: if you revert, also add a quick SG ingress from the NAT gw ip range or the cluster ENI cidr to sg-07a1b2c3 so we get traffic through while Terraform changes propagate. After revert, I'll run curl tests from multiple AZ pods and watch 5xx/connection metrics.

Mason: reverting PR and reapplying explicit endpoint-hosted-zone association + sg rule. patch: 
```
hashicorp/terraform apply -target=aws_vpc_endpoint.vpce_models_api
# re-add aws_vpc_endpoint_dns_entry and aws_security_group_rule for sg-07a1b2c3 allowing 10.1.0.0/16->443
```

Eli: nice — once that's applied, check from a pod: 
```
curl -v https://models-api.internal.redwood/health || true
traceroute -n 10.0.5.23
```
and post the outputs here. I'll keep an eye on L7 LB error graphs.

Mason: :thumbsup: revert applied, association re-created and SG rule added. running curl and traceroute now — will update in 3m.

SRE-Robin: after you confirm, follow up by adding an assertion to the infra test harness that validates: endpoint hosted zone association + SG ingress for cluster cidrs, so this doesn't regress on future route-table cleanups.

Mason: yep creating a short test now and will open a follow-up PR to harden the TF module. thanks all.
